title: encodeDelta
body:
## encodeDelta

Compress a changed snapshot relative to a captured earlier snapshot, retaining the reference needed for restoration.

Native binding: `zstd --patch-from=REFERENCE`. Output kind: `["file","text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | Absolute local regular file to capture. Compression and comparison treat it as original bytes; restoration and frame inspection treat it as a compressed stream. Dictionary inspection treats it as exact dictionary bytes. Changing bytes at the same path invalidates reuse. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
| `format` | Zstandard is the default. gzip, xz, lzma and lz4 provide compatibility with other readers; Zstandard-only controls are refused for those formats. | `{"type":"enum","values":["zstd","gzip","xz","lzma","lz4"]}` | `"zstd"` |
| `level` | Higher levels generally spend more CPU and memory to reduce file size, with identical decoded content. Zstandard permits 1–22; compatibility codecs permit 1–9. Use fast acceleration instead of an explicit level when speed dominates. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":22}` | `3` |
| `fast` | A positive value selects the native fast mode; larger values favour speed over compressed size. Zero uses the level. Supplying both a positive acceleration and an explicit level is refused. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":100}` | `0` |
| `threads` | One or two native compression workers. This is distinct from single-thread I/O; ordinary one-worker mode can still use asynchronous I/O. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":2}` | `1` |
| `singleThread` | Use the native strictly single-thread implementation. It requires one worker and cannot be combined with rsyncable compression. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
| `checksum` | Write the low 32 bits of XXH64 over decoded content into every Zstandard frame. The host independently recomputes it after fresh decoding. This detects accidental corruption; it is not an authenticity signature. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
| `dictionaryID` | Include the dictionary numeric ID in frame headers. Turning this off does not embed the dictionary or remove its dependency; retain the exact captured dictionary. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
| `longWindowLog` | Zero disables long-distance matching. A value 10–27 enables it with a window measured as 2 to this power in bytes; larger windows require more decoder memory. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":27}` | `0` |
| `rsyncable` | Enable native rsyncable block selection to reduce retransmission after file changes. It trades some compression efficiency for more stable boundaries and requires the worker-based implementation. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
| `literals` | Let Zstandard choose, force compressed literals, or force raw literals. This controls unreferenced bytes inside blocks rather than whether the entire file is compressed. | `{"type":"enum","values":["automatic","compressed","raw"]}` | `"automatic"` |
| `chunkBytes` | Zero creates one frame. A positive byte count cuts the captured source into independently compressed frames; at most 256 are permitted. This aids bounded access but may reduce compression across boundaries. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":67108864}` | `0` |
| `streamInput` | Feed finite captured content through standard input. Its frame omits content size unless an exact pledgedBytes value is supplied. Actual decoded bytes remain bounded and checked. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
| `tuning` | Named native match-finder overrides to the chosen compression level. Omit this object for the native preset; unsupported keys and arbitrary command arguments are refused. | `{"type":"object","properties":{"windowLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":10,"maximum":27},"chainLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":6,"maximum":26},"hashLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":6,"maximum":25},"searchLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":20},"minMatch":{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":7},"targetLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":999},"strategy":{"type":"enum","values":["fast","doubleFast","greedy","lazy","lazy2","btlazy2","btopt","btultra","btultra2"]},"overlapLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":9},"ldmHashRateLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":20},"ldmHashLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":6,"maximum":24},"ldmMinMatch":{"type":"integer","minimum":4,"maximum":4096},"ldmBucketSizeLog":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":8}}}` | `{}` |
| `dictionary` | Select exact trained dictionary bytes or raw history bytes using dictionaryMode. A numeric dictionary ID is not a cryptographic identity. A dictionary and a delta reference are alternative dependency mechanisms. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | omitted |
| `dictionaryMode` | Trained dictionaries include the Zstandard magic header and numeric identifier. Raw dictionaries are nonempty history bytes without that header and use dictionary ID zero. Both require exact retained bytes for restoration. | `{"type":"enum","values":["trained","raw"]}` | `"trained"` |
| `contentSize` | Automatic includes a known file size and omits an unknown stream size. Omit suppresses the frame size. Require needs an exact pledgedBytes value for a standard-input stream. Actual decoded output remains bounded in every mode. | `{"type":"enum","values":["automatic","omit","require"]}` | `"automatic"` |
| `pledgedBytes` | Exact total source bytes for one standard-input frame. The captured byte count must match before native execution. A pledge cannot be combined with chunking or an approximate size hint. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":67108864}` | omitted |
| `sizeHintBytes` | Hint used to select compression parameters for a standard-input stream. It does not assert the actual size or remove decoded-output limits. Use pledgedBytes when an exact frame size is required. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":67108864}` | omitted |
| `targetBlockBytes` | Zero uses the native default. A positive value asks for an approximate compressed block size, 64–131072 bytes. It is a compression target rather than an exact block-size or random-access guarantee. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":131072}` | `0` |
| `jobBytes` | Zero uses automatic worker scheduling. A positive value requires an explicit tuning.windowLog or longWindowLog and covers at least 512 KiB and the selected history overlap. Automatic overlap reserves the full window so native scheduling cannot silently increase an undersized request. It requires worker-based I/O. Delta encoding derives its window from captured sizes and refuses explicit job-size overrides. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":67108864}` | `0` |
| `adaptive` | Let native Zstandard adjust compression effort within named level bounds as throughput changes. Bounds must include the initial level and require worker-based compression. Native adaptation is not reproducible; verification proves content and frame policy, not the historical level schedule. | `{"type":"object","properties":{"minLevel":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":22,"default":1},"maxLevel":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":22,"default":19}}}` | omitted |
| `reference` | Select the earlier complete byte sequence used by delta compression. Restoration needs the exact same reference; it is retained as a captured dependency. In a workflow, a pinned adopted file or an explicitly selected directory-snapshot member can supply these bytes; changing its captured content is refused. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | **required** |
